findings.claim: The diff changes routers/admin_markdown_images.py and routers/uploads.py, and it moves many handlers onto asyncio.to_thread (drive folder handlers, batch_move, rename/move endpoints, batch_rename, empty_trash, purge_all_missing). None of these files or handlers is in the touch-point list.
findings.impact: The admin Markdown image-import endpoint now splits start_import into prepare_import and launch_import and runs prepare_import in a worker thread. uploads.complete_upload also runs in a thread. These are behaviour and concurrency changes beyond path resolution. In particular, a SQLAlchemy Session and the module-global _current_job_id are now touched from worker threads.
findings.evidence: backend/app/routers/admin_markdown_images.py:70-80 (asyncio.to_thread(prepare_import ...) then launch_import); backend/app/routers/uploads.py:84; backend/app/routers/drives.py (to_thread on create_folder, rename_folder, move_folder, delete_folder, purge_all_trash, purge_all_missing); backend/app/routers/files.py (batch_move, batch_rename, rename_file_endpoint, move_file_endpoint).

bucket_proposal.reason: No declared invariant is broken. The spec section 10 says no scandir may run on the event loop, which motivates the threading, but the touch-point list does not name these files. Unplanned scope.

findings.proposed_fix: Add these files to the touch-point list, or revert the thread offloading where it is not needed.

findings.claim: docs/ADDON-DEVELOPMENT.md is edited but is not in the touch-point list. The spec text mentions it only in the user-visible behavior section.

bucket_proposal.reason: Not an invariant. Unplanned touch point.

findings.claim: physical_delete now raises HTTPException 409 for an ambiguous name partway through a batch loop. In purge_all_trash and purge_all_missing, files earlier in the loop are already unlinked from disk but their rows are not yet committed.
findings.impact: One ambiguous file aborts the batch. Earlier files are gone from disk while their rows stay in Trash or Missing until the user purges again. The re-purge succeeds because the unlink is skipped when the file is absent. The trash purge job in main.py has the same exposure, depending on how it handles the exception.

bucket_proposal.reason: I12 requires 409 and no change for the ambiguous file itself. It does not cover batch partial-state behaviour.

findings.claim: complete_upload resolves the leaf with a non-strict resolve_on_disk. If an NFD twin of the target appeared after init_upload, the upload replaces that existing file in place.
findings.impact: This is a rare race. The spec's step 6 allows replacement in place, so it is probably intended, but no test covers the complete step.

bucket_proposal.reason: Probably matches spec step 6. Edge case with no test.

specification_compliance: Touch-point question answered: the diff reaches routers/admin_markdown_images.py, routers/uploads.py, the to_thread offloading of the drives.py folder and trash handlers, and the files.py batch_move, batch_rename, rename and move endpoints. It also reaches docs/ADDON-DEVELOPMENT.md. None of these is in the list. tests/test_listing_call_inventory.py is a test and is treated as implicit.
The resolver contract in diskpath.py matches I3, I4 and I12 on a read of the code: exact path first, dot and empty components match nothing, strict raises AmbiguousPath, and nothing is written.
The addon invariants I14 to I16 and the parity table are out of this commit's scope. I did not find a parity fixture in this diff.
potential_unspecified_behavior: start_import is split into prepare_import and launch_import, with the preparation run in a worker thread.
Handlers that previously ran on the event loop now run in worker threads, using the shared SQLAlchemy session.
_checked_inside in drives.py imports the private safepath._contains_symlink, which the spec says is intended.
regression_risks: The db Session is passed into worker threads. Sequential use is probably fine, but any code still on the loop that touches the same session concurrently could race.
A cached read path is confirmed by lexists only. A replacement file at the same spelling is fine, but the cache is shared by all readers.
Non-strict readers pick the first match while mutating sites refuse. The two can disagree on a twin pair.
test_coverage: Strong coverage of I1 to I12 through a layout matrix (leaf, ancestor, both), including ambiguity 409 and batch rollback.
The inventory test has a seeded-detector self-check, but LISTING_DERIVED is empty and the DRIVE_PART regex is heuristic, so a join with an unusual variable name can be missed.
No tests for the thread offloading, for batch purge partial failure, or for the complete_upload resolve.
not_verified: I did not run any tests. The tools are read-only.
I did not read the full bodies of the fileops mutators, the main.py purge job exception handling, or the scanner change.
I did not inspect the addon repositories or the parity fixture.
I did not check the thread-safety of SQLAlchemy session use under the to_thread calls.
